neighbours.label: fabric that dresses a household surface: words for coverings of beds, windows, tables and chairs (bedspread, drapes, quilt, runner)
fire: On the guest bed she laid a folded bedspread of white cotton.
He hemmed new curtains and a pair of pillowcases for the cottage.
Grandma stitched a crib quilt from old scraps of flannel.
They replaced the roller shades with heavy linen drapes.
A crocheted table runner lay beneath the candlesticks.
Mother draped an embroidered throw over the armchair.
The inn's rooms had chenille bedspreads and ruffled valances.
Each chair back was protected by a lace antimacassar.
quiet: On the guest desk she laid a folded map of the island.
He installed new shelves and a pair of reading lamps for the cottage.
Grandma carved a toy boat from old scraps of cedar.
They replaced the kitchen faucets with heavy brass fittings.
A polished silver tray lay beneath the candlesticks.
Mother placed an antique clock on the mantel.
The inn's rooms had oak dressers and small writing desks.
Each chair leg was reinforced by a steel bracket.

notes: Top examples are coverlet, duvet, afghan and blinds. Probes on new cases (quilt, valance, doily, slipcover) reached 0.52-0.63, while hard furniture stayed under 0.25. Venetian blinds in the card show it is not strictly about fabric. Fire items use cases outside the top examples where possible.
